answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a copper-denominated bond before it may trade or vote, then slash that bond when independent counterparties expose collusion. Reputation grows only through signed transactions with established agents, sampled by random audits across the ocean of activity; cloned identities start with no trust and cannot cheaply manufacture history. A mirror check compares claims across unrelated neighborhoods. A Sybil attacker must fund every persona and risk losing its stake, making scale expensive.
